title: Vaginal Bleeding
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} is a reproductive-age woman presenting with irregular, heavy vaginal bleeding without identifiable structural or systemic cause. This is dysfunctional uterine bleeding (DUB), most commonly anovulatory — unopposed estrogen stimulation leads to endometrial hyperplasia and irregular shedding. Diagnosis of exclusion after ruling out pregnancy, structural lesions (fibroids, polyps), thyroid dysfunction, coagulopathy, and malignancy. Workup: HCG (rule out pregnancy/complications), CBC (assess anemia from blood loss), TSH/prolactin, pelvic ultrasound (rule out structural causes), endometrial biopsy if age >45 or risk factors. Treatment depends on severity and fertility goals: hormonal regulation with combined OCPs or cyclic progestins. If acute heavy bleeding: high-dose estrogen or IV conjugated estrogens. Iron supplementation for anemia.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Abdomen
stacks.finding: Assess for pelvic mass or tenderness.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Genitalia / Pelvic / Speculum
stacks.finding: Visualize source of bleeding. Bimanual exam for uterine size, adnexal masses.

stacks.label: HCG, beta (pregnancy test)
stacks.finding: MUST rule out pregnancy — ectopic, miscarriage, molar pregnancy can all present with vaginal bleeding.

stacks.label: CBC with differential
stacks.finding: Assess degree of anemia from blood loss. Platelet count.

stacks.label: TSH / Prolactin
stacks.finding: Thyroid dysfunction and hyperprolactinemia cause anovulatory bleeding.

stacks.label: PT/PTT / INR
stacks.finding: Screen for coagulopathy (von Willebrand disease can present with menorrhagia).

stacks.label: Pelvic ultrasound (transvaginal)
stacks.finding: Rule out fibroids, polyps, adenomyosis, ovarian masses. Assess endometrial thickness.

stacks.label: Endometrial biopsy
stacks.finding: Indicated if age >45, unopposed estrogen exposure, or risk factors for endometrial hyperplasia/cancer.

stacks.label: BMP / CMP / LFTs
stacks.finding: Screening labs. Iron studies if anemic.

stacks.label: Combined oral contraceptives
stacks.finding: Hormonal regulation. Estrogen-progestin combination stabilizes endometrium and regulates cycles.

stacks.label: Iron supplementation
stacks.finding: Treat iron deficiency anemia from chronic blood loss.

physical_exam.genitourinary: Vaginal bleeding on speculum. No cervical lesions. Bimanual: normal uterus, no adnexal masses.

decoys.label: Hysterectomy as first-line
decoys.reason_wrong: DUB responds to medical management (OCPs, cyclic progestins). Surgery reserved for failed medical therapy or completed childbearing.

teach_me_steps.reasoning: Rule out pregnancy (HCG), structural (US), thyroid (TSH), prolactin, coagulopathy (PT/PTT). Anovulatory = unopposed estrogen → endometrial proliferation → irregular shedding.

teach_me_steps.order: Medical management: OCPs or cyclic progestins
teach_me_steps.reasoning: Hormonal regulation stabilizes endometrium. Iron for anemia. EM biopsy if age >45 or risk factors for hyperplasia.

case_summary: Anovulatory DUB. HCG negative, normal pelvic US, normal TSH. CBC shows iron deficiency anemia. OCPs for cycle regulation + iron supplementation. EM biopsy if indicated by age/risk.
